hero: A US men's 10 = UK 9 = EU 43 = JP/CM 28. The 8.47 mm step between sizes comes from the medieval English 'barleycorn' (⅓ inch). Japanese sizing uses foot length in centimetres directly — the cleanest system.
body: Shoe sizing is one of the few metrology systems where the imperial origin (barleycorns, 1324 English statute) is still baked into modern products. US and UK both use the ⅓-inch step; EU uses the Paris point (⅔ cm ≈ 6.67 mm); Japan and Korea use Mondopoint (foot length in mm or cm). Same foot, up to four sticker sizes.
## The exact factors

> 1 barleycorn = 1/3 inch = 8.4667 mm
> UK sizing: size 0 at 4 inches, +1 barleycorn per size
> US men's = UK + 1 (empirically)
> US women's = US men's + 1.5 (Brannock convention)
> EU (Paris point): size = length(mm) × 3/2, +2
> Japan (Mondopoint): size = foot length in cm
> Half sizes step 4.23 mm

**The 1.5-size men-to-women rule:** in the US, a men's 8 fits like a women's 9.5. The width and last shape may differ, but the length is identical. Unisex sneakers (Chuck Taylors, Vans) use this bridge — a women's 9 buyer picks men's 7.5.
## Kids' sizing — three subranges
**Infant/toddler (0–3 y):** US 0–10 (baby), length 8–16.5 cm. EU uses the same Paris-point system with kid sizes 16–27.
**Trap:** US kids' 7 ≠ US men's 7. A kids' 7 is length 25.4 cm; a men's 7 is 24.6 cm. Kids' sizes are labelled with 'Y' (youth) or 'C' (child) to disambiguate — but often aren't on cheaper labels.
## Where the barleycorn came from

In 1324, King Edward II standardised the English inch as three barleycorns end-to-end. The shoemaker guilds already sized by barleycorn: size 13 = 13 inches / 3 = 4.33 inches foot length + a starting offset. This size 13 was set as the boundary between kids' and adults' — which is why the US 'largest kids' size' is still 13.5–3 today. The system persists 700 years later because retail inertia is enormous.
## The Mondopoint alternative

ISO 9407:2019 defines Mondopoint: foot length in millimetres, plus width grade. A shoe labelled 'Mondopoint 275/95' fits a foot 275 mm long, 95 mm wide. Used by military boots, ski boots, and Japanese/Korean retail. Cleanest sizing possible — no unit conversion needed. Growing adoption in athletic footwear.
## How to measure your foot
1. Stand on a piece of A4 paper with heel against a wall.
2. Mark the longest toe (usually the second, not the big toe) on the paper.
3. Measure heel-to-mark in mm. Add 5 mm ease.
4. Look up in the table above — for either foot separately; feet differ 3–8 mm.
5. Buy for the larger foot. Insole spacers fit the smaller.
Best time to measure: end of day, when feet are 4–7% larger than morning.
## Width designations

US uses letters: 2A (narrow) < B (women's medium) < D (men's medium) < 2E (wide) < 4E (extra wide). UK uses similar. EU width sizing is inconsistent — some brands use letters (F/G/H), others print 'Weite +' or numeric. Nike, Adidas, and most sneakers only stock D/medium; specialty brands (New Balance, Brooks) carry the full width range.
## Cross-border shopping gotchas
- **UK to US men's:** add 1 whole size.
- **US men's to EU:** multiply by 2.5 then add 34, roughly.
- **US men's to JP:** subtract 18.
- **US men's to women's:** add 1.5.
- **Nike vs Adidas:** Adidas runs 0.5 size larger than Nike, worldwide. New Balance runs true to length but wider.
- **Asian sizing on AliExpress:** almost always 1 full size smaller than the Western label claims. Ordering a 'US 10' from a Chinese seller often arrives as a US 9.
## The five-second recap

Measure foot length in mm. US = your foot length in mm / 8.47 minus an offset (roughly - 26 for men, - 24.5 for women). Or just use the table. Best system: Mondopoint (mm foot length). Worst mistake: buying Asian-sized without dropping a size.

faqs.q: Is US shoe size the same as UK?
faqs.a: No. US men's = UK + 1. US women's = UK + 2. This has been the case since the systems diverged in the early 20th century; UK stayed on the 1880 sizing baseline while the US shifted.

faqs.q: Why is EU size a bigger number than US?
faqs.a: EU uses the Paris point (⅔ cm = 6.67 mm) as its size step, and starts numbering from length zero (no offset). Sizes grow faster on the number line but represent the same physical length as US/UK.
ISO 9407 sizing: foot length in mm (or cm) plus width in mm. Used for ski boots, military boots, and increasingly athletic footwear. A '275/95' fits a 275 mm long, 95 mm wide foot.

faqs.q: How much should shoes be bigger than my foot?
faqs.a: 3–10 mm ease at the longest toe. Zero ease pinches on downhill walking; too much lets the foot slide and blister. Athletic shoes tend to the larger end; dress shoes the smaller.

faqs.q: Do feet change size with age?
faqs.a: Yes. Ligaments stretch, arches flatten, feet lengthen 5–10 mm over adulthood. Most people wear the same size their entire adult life without remeasuring — and get feet 1 size longer than the shoe fits.
